feed.title: Combined summary - Standardizing public key exposure classification for existing outputs

entry.title: Combined summary - Standardizing public key exposure classification for existing outputs
entry.summary: The ongoing discussions and developments in the classification of Bitcoin outputs based on their exposure level present significant advancements in the cryptocurrency's security protocols. The proposed specification targets the classification of Bitcoin outputs by determining whether the public key required for spending has been published on-chain. This initiative addresses a gap left by BIP 360 and BIP 361, which do not specify how to ascertain the exposure status of existing outputs. Estimates suggest that exposed supplies could range from 25% to over 34%, highlighting the necessity for a standardized approach to enhance consistency across different tools and platforms. The draft specification introduces four distinct exposure levels: EXPOSED_AT_REST, EXPOSED_ON_SPEND, NOT_EXPOSED, and UNDETERMINED. These classifications are assigned based on available data with a fail-closed rule applied when data is insufficient, ensuring the safer assumption of higher exposure. This structure aims to prevent discrepancies that arise due to the varying capacities of tools to track and classify output types, particularly newer or unrecognized ones. The proposal includes a constant-time floor requirement to mitigate errors in exposure classification caused by incomplete historical data scans. Significant revisions and feedback have shaped the evolution of this draft, now versioned at 0.5.1 and submitted as an Informational BIP. Changes in recent updates include clarifications in the definitions of exposure levels, particularly distinguishing between 'attacker-spendability' and 'holder-provability'. These adjustments stem from community feedback, emphasizing real-world application errors and theoretical ambiguities. The draft and its continual refinement, documented through various versions ([Reference implementation and test vectors](https://github.com/duncan0k/pubkey-exposure-classification)), underscore the collaborative effort to standardize how exposure is assessed, moving towards a more secure and predictable framework for Bitcoin transactions. Each iteration of the draft, including the feedback loops from platforms like Delving Bitcoin ([discussion thread](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/standardizing-an-exposure-classification-for-existing-outputs-pre-bip/2866)), reflects a comprehensive approach to addressing both technical and conceptual challenges. The discourse around these updates not only enriches the understanding but also ensures that the classification system remains robust against evolving threats and technologies in the digital currency landscape. As this specification progresses towards potentially becoming a BIP, the focus remains on aligning all tools to a common standard that reliably reflects the security status of Bitcoin outputs based on observable data.
